title: Ocean acidification reduces diatom and photosynthetic gene abundance on plastic in an coastal bay mesocosm experiment.
content:
Abstract

Discarded plastics are accumulating in the global ocean and posing threats to marine life. The plastisphere - the community colonizing plastic surfaces - profoundly influences the environmental behavior of plastic, affecting its degradation and entry into marine food webs. Ocean acidification (OA) due to anthropogenic CO2 emissions, is also threatening marine ecosystems, but the effect of OA on the structure and ecological functions of plastisphere communities remain poorly understood. Here, using a mesocosm experiment, we investigated the effects of OA on the plastisphere colonizing floating PET plastic bottles. The study was conducted using subtropical eutrophic coastal water from Southern China under two CO2 conditions: increased CO2 to 1000 μatm (HC) and ambient CO2 410 μatm (LC). Metagenomic sequencing of the plastic samples, after exposure for 32 days, showed striking changes in relative abundance of eukaryotes and bacteria caused by HC. There was a 75.3 % decrease in eukaryote read abundances at high CO2, most strikingly a 95.6% decrease in the relative abundance of diatoms. In addition, the relative abundance of genes involved in photosystem II light reactions and pigment synthesis decreased under high CO2 conditions. This suggests that OA could reduce the photosynthetic potential of the plastisphere. Shifts in plastisphere community structure and potentially diminished photosynthesis under OA could influence food chains within plastisphere, plastic degradation, transportation, and carbon cycling involving plastics. Overall, our results suggest that OA can alter the functional ecology of the plastisphere, with potential implications for marine biogeochemical processes and food web dynamics in subtropical eutrophic coastal water.

Keywords:

Marine plastic pollution; Metagenome; Microbial communities; Ocean acidification; Plastisphere.

title: Unraveling the occurrence and fate of organo(thio)phosphate esters through municipal wastewater treatment based on nontarget screening and mass balance calculation.
content:
Abstract

The release of organophosphate esters (OPEs) and their analogues, organothiophosphate esters (OTPEs), from wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) has raised growing concern due to their potential ecological risks. However, the structural profiles and environmental behavior of these emerging contaminants, collectively referred to as O(T)PEs, remain poorly understood during wastewater treatment. In this study, we employed suspect and nontarget screening to investigate the occurrence and fate of 57 O(T)PEs throughout a full‑scale municipal wastewater treatment process. The identified compounds include 26 organophosphate triesters, 11 organophosphate diesters, 6 organothiophosphate triesters, and 14 organothiophosphate diesters (di‑OTPEs). Notably, 20 compounds were detected for the first time in wastewater or sludge, 13 of which were newly identified. Across treatment stages, the total O(T)PE concentrations ranged from 1021 to 1589 ng/L in the aqueous phase and from 2423 to 30,134 ng/g dry weight in the solid phase. The mass loading of O(T)PEs entering the WWTP was estimated at 1282 g/day (equivalent to 5.6 mg per capita per day), with 8.0% discharged in the final effluent and 13% retained in dewatered sludge. Mass balance analysis revealed that sludge adsorption enables effective removal of hydrophobic O(T)PEs, whereas the removal of polar O(T)PEs primarily relies on biodegradation. Moreover, despite the multiplicative increase in di‑OTPE concentrations caused by biological treatment, the subsequent ultraviolet disinfection unit could enable their effective removal. This study delineates the behavior and removal pathways of O(T)PEs in a typical municipal WWTP and provides a scientific basis for future upgrades in wastewater treatment.

Keywords:

Mass flow; Municipal wastewater; Organothiophosphate esters; Removal pathways; Sludge; Suspect and nontarget analysis.

title: Deciphering the mechanisms shaping the antibiotic resistance genes in the vertical plastisphere in hyporheic zone under hydrological exchange.
content:
Abstract

Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) prevalence has raised increasing concern due to their potential risks for ecological safety and human health. Although the plastisphere has been recognized as a hotspot for ARG spread, little is known about how the hydrological exchange reshapes ARG dissemination in plastisphere, which frequently occurs in the hyporheic zone (HZ) with its vertical upwelling and downwelling flows. To fill this knowledge gap, this study investigated ARG propagation in vertically distributed plastispheres within HZ under various hydrological exchange scenarios. Results showed that hydrological exchange lowered ARG abundance in the HZ plastisphere. Vertically, upwelling shifted the ARG enrichment pattern toward the surface plastisphere, whereas ARGs were bottom-enriched under no-water exchange. In addition, hydrological exchange reassembled microbial communities in plastisphere, with upwelling leading to higher microbial species richness and diversity. Notably, the upwelling plastisphere substantially enriched nitrifying bacteria and genes, exhibiting negative effects on ARG spread. Compared with surface plastisphere, the ARGs-host interactions were more complex in the bottom plastisphere, and upwelling weakened the complexity. Moreover, the ARG abundance in the plastisphere was significantly and positively correlated with mobile genetic element (MGE) abundance (Pearson's R = 0.687-0.997, P < 0.05), indicating a high potential of horizontal gene transfer (HGT) that is mainly regulated by transposase and integrase. Overall, N-cycling and HGT jointly regulated ARG dissemination in the HZ plastisphere under hydrological exchange, but exerted opposite effects with N-cycling acting as a suppressive factor whereas HGT promoted ARG propagation. These findings provide new insights into the ARGs propagation in the plastisphere in HZ, highlighting the significant roles of hydrological exchange on antimicrobial resistance under increasing global nitrate pollution in groundwater.

Keywords:

Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs); Hydrological exchange; Hyporheic zone (HZ); Nitrogen cycling; Plastisphere.

title: DeepLab-AFOS: A marine oil spill detection method based on advantageous features from polarimetric SAR.
content:
Abstract

Marine oil spills can severely damage marine ecosystems and cause significant economic losses. Accurate detection and extraction represent the most critical and fundamental requirements for marine oil spill monitoring and emergency response. While the application of SAR in marine oil spill detection has been extensively studied, most existing works rely solely on SAR backscattering information, with limited integration of polarimetric and textural features. This insufficiency often leads to difficulties in distinguishing oil spills from look-alikes. To address the challenge of differentiating oil spills from look-alikes, we constructed an advantageous features dual-polarimetric SAR dataset (AF-OS), incorporating multidimensional features such as covariance matrices, polarimetric parameters, and textural descriptors. Based on this dataset, we proposed a polarimetric SAR oil spill detection method named DeepLab-AFOS. Comparative experiments using datasets with different feature combinations demonstrate that the features included in AF-OS significantly enhance the accuracy of oil spill extraction. Furthermore, model comparison results show that DeepLab-AFOS outperforms models such as U-Net, PSP-Net, ResNet-UNet, Segmenter-B, OSDMamba and DeepLabV3+, achieving an accuracy of 97.2%, F1 score of 95.8%, and MIoU of 92.06%. Additionally, we applied DeepLab-AFOS to a real-world oil spill event in the Gulf of Mexico. The extracted results were consistent with ground-truth validation, accurately identifying the oil spill and effectively distinguishing it from look-alikes. Both AF-OS and DeepLab-AFOS provide effective solutions for the accurate extraction of marine oil spills.

Keywords:

Advantageous features dataset; DeepLab; Dual-polarimetric SAR; Oil spill detection.

title: Dual-layered epigenetic regulation links water body size constraints to somatic growth in an allotetraploid fish.
content:
Abstract

Polyploidy endows fish with genomic plasticity to colonize restricted environments, yet the molecular mechanisms linking ecological constraints to somatic growth remain elusive. Here, we investigated the adaptive response of an allotetraploid lineage (Carassius auratus × Cyprinus carpio) to contrasting water body sizes using multi-omics approaches. We found that spatial constraints triggered targeted transcriptional remodeling specifically in the eye and muscle. This response effectively links sensory perception to growth regulation. Meanwhile, we identified a dual-layered epigenetic strategy. Environmental stress forced a reduction in the active gene pool via promoter silencing, while concurrently depressing the expression levels of growth-related structural genes through enhancer inhibition. Interestingly, this plasticity exhibited striking subgenome asymmetry. The Cyprinus subgenome displayed higher epigenetic responsiveness and acted as the primary adaptive buffer, exemplified by the targeted repression of a Cyprinus-derived enhancer regulating the mTOR gene rps6kb1a. Our findings demonstrate how subgenome-biased epigenetic remodeling aligns growth phenotypes with ecological constraints, offering molecular insights into the evolutionary success of polyploids in fragmented habitats.

Keywords:

Allotetraploid fish; Body size divergence; Chromatin accessibility; Environmental adaptation; Subgenome.

title: Sibship Size and Academic Achievement in the PISA 2022 Survey.
content:
Abstract

Introduction:

The influence of siblinghood on psychosocial development has long been a topic of focus in developmental psychology. Prior research, however, has yielded conflicting conclusions: some studies argue that siblinghood dilutes family resources, thereby impeding individuals' academic success, while others hold that competition and cooperation among siblings can effectively boost the development of socio-cognitive abilities. Drawing on the conditional resource dilution model and ecological systems theory, this study globally examines the role of siblinghood and the moderating effects of family wealth, national economic conditions, and cultural contexts.

Methods:

Data from PISA 2022 included 570,937 15-year-old adolescents (Mage = 15.79, SDage = 0.29) from 77 countries. Analyses examined the relationship between sibship size and academic achievement, and the moderating effects of family wealth (student-level), GDP, and cultural individualism (national-level).

Results:

Adolescents with one sibling outperformed only-children and those with two or more siblings. Family wealth amplified the positive effect of having one sibling and buffered the negative effect of having two or more siblings. Multilevel modeling revealed that GDP positively moderated the interaction between sibship size and family wealth. Similarly, individualism positively moderated this effect in families with two or more children.

Conclusions:

This study reveals a nonlinear relationship between sibship size and academic achievement. In two-child households, siblings may not significantly dilute resources but function as resources that facilitate academic development. The dilution effect increases significantly when sibship size exceeds two. Family wealth moderates these effects, which are further amplified by national wealth and individualism.

Keywords:

GDP; PISA; adolescents' academic achievement; ecological systems theory; resource dilution; sibship size.

author.name: Qingke Guo 1 2 3 , Jing Liao 1 , Bo Yang

title: Water-evaporation-induced efficient high-temperature aerobic fermentation of food waste.
content:
Abstract

Aerobic fermentation is an effective approach for reducing, stabilising, and recovering resources from food waste. However, its performance is often constrained by poor oxygen transfer within the fermentation substrate. In this study, we investigated the inductive mechanism of water evaporation enhancing aerobic fermentation of food waste. It was observed that water evaporation, as the primary driving force, promoted microscale moisture redistribution and pore structure optimization, leading to an 84.8% (p < 0.01) increase in the average pore diameter and an 8.7% (p < 0.01) increase in porosity. As a result, a significant increase in the oxygen mass transfer coefficient (+250.1%) was achieved within the food waste. This improved microenvironment steered microbial community succession toward thermophilic functional groups dominated by Bacillus and Diutina, prolonging the thermophilic phase by 167% (p < 0.05) and facilitating the degradation of major organic components. Among them, the degradation rate of lipids was significantly increased by 57.1% (p < 0.01). Consequently, the humic substance content in the fermentation product increased by 18.8% (p < 0.05) and the corresponding germination index increased by 41.4% (p < 0.05). These results were further confirmed by the metagenomic analysis, which indicated that water evaporation induced the significant enrichment of functional genes associated with the tricarboxylic acid cycle and electron transport chain in the aerobic fermentation. These findings offer new mechanistic insights into leveraging microscale moisture regulation to optimize aerobic bioconversion.

Keywords:

Foodwaste; High-temperature aerobic fermentation; Humification; Oxygen transfer.

title: Physiological responses of Mediterranean octocorals to prolonged exposure to ecologically relevant microplastic concentrations.
content:
Abstract

Microplastics (MPs) are pervasive contaminants in the Mediterranean Sea, yet their long-term effects on habitat-forming octocorals remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally evaluated the physiological responses of the gorgonians Eunicella singularis and Paramuricea clavata after three months of exposure to a mixture of PET, PS, and PP particles. Respiration, feeding performance, organic matter content, MP ingestion and histological condition were assessed at the end of the experiment. MP exposure significantly reduced respiration rates in both species, indicating metabolic depression and potential energy-conservation responses, while prey capture and organic matter content remained stable. Both gorgonians ingested MPs, dominated by PET, with species-specific differences in particle number and size retention. No tissue damage or structural alterations were detected, suggesting effective clearance rather than long-term retention. Overall, prolonged exposure produced limited physiological impairment, although metabolic adjustments may represent sublethal energetic trade-offs with implications for long-term resilience under future stress scenarios.

Keywords:

Benthic organisms; Eunicella singularis; Gorgonians; Paramuricea clavata; Plastic; Pollution.

title: Low and steady: Minimal change in plastic exposure in Kermadec Petrels in the remote South Pacific.
content:
Abstract

Plastic pollution is increasing in our oceans, and while exposure is also increasing in many wild species, there are exceptions. Understanding which species are at risk is therefore important to identifying conservation priorities and responding to the pollution crisis. Here, we document ingested plastics in Kermadec Petrels (Pterodroma neglecta) on uninhabited Henderson Island and Oeno Atoll in the remote South Pacific and compare our results with historical data. While sample sizes are limited, the data suggests plastic ingestion has remained consistent over >30 years, with 23.1% of fledglings (n = 13) sampled in 2025 containing small quantities of plastics (mean ± SD: 0.0113 ± 0.0061 g, median pieces 2.0). These data contrast with plastic ingestion records for other closely related species in the region, suggesting Kermadec Petrels can selectively avoid consuming plastic, or forage in locations with lower plastic densities, and are therefore at less risk of exposure.

Keywords:

Foraging ecology; Ingested plastic; Interspecific variation; Microplastic; Plastic pollution; Seabirds; gadfly petrel.

author.name: Jennifer L Lavers 1 , Jacqui Christian 2 , Alexander L Bond

title: Oxidative Stress Biomarkers in the Shrimp Macrobrachium amazonicum (Heller, 1862): Assessment in an Environmental Preservation Area in the Brazilian Amazon.
content:
Abstract

Anthropogenic activities generate a significant amount of pollutants that are released into the environment, causing physiological and ecological disturbances. Among the xenobiotics present in aquatic ecosystems, numerous chemical and organic compounds have oxidative potential or are metabolized through oxidative processes, which may amplify the damage caused by reactive oxygen species to biological systems. The quantification of cellular damage and antioxidant defenses can be used as biomarkers for early aquatic contamination. The aim of this research was to use the shrimp Macrobrachium amazonicum as a bioindicator species to assess oxidative damage caused by xenobiotics in an Environmental Protection Area in the Brazilian Amazon. The analyses evaluated physicochemical parameters, Iron, Copper, Total Solids, pH, and Temperature, as well as non-enzymatic and enzymatic oxidative stress biomarkers: Thiobarbituric Acid Reactive Substances, glutathione (GSH), and catalase (CAT) in hepatopancreas homogenates. Among the analyzed metals, only copper (Cu) showed a statistically significant influence on GSH and CAT activities, whereas the other parameters did not exhibit significant effects. Oxidative stress parameters can be important tools in biomonitoring work, helping to understand the effects of contamination on aquatic organisms and providing important information on cellular defense modulations.

Keywords:

Amazon River; biological marker; crustacean; oxidative inhibitor; pollutant agent.

title: A novel fluorescence method for sensitive detection of amikacin residues in milk samples: Greenness, blueness, and redness assessment.
content:
Abstract

Amikacin is an antibiotic commonly employed in veterinary medicine primarily for treatment and prevention of certain diseases. This study describes sensitive and simple spectrofluorimetric approach for the detection of amikacin in real milk samples that adopts a one pot-synthesis of a fully conjugated, planar, and cationic diarylpyrrolone derivative, this fluorogenic reaction allows sensitive determination of amikacin in milk at an emission wavelength of 485 nm after excitation at 390 nm, for the first time. The limits of detection and quantification were 20.60 and 62.50ngmL-1, respectively over a concentration range of 80.0-400.0, with good recovery. The facile application of the proposed method paves the way for its implementation in monitoring the potential risks posed by residual antibiotics to public health and ecological integrity.

Keywords:

Amikacin; Diarylpyrrolone derivative; Fluorescence method; Milk.

title: Deciphering Mn(II)/peroxymonosulfate system with nitrilotriacetic acid to degrade antibiotics: Roles of Mn species and interference of protein-like DOM.
content:
Abstract

Aquaculture activities discharge large amounts of antibiotics, with protein-like dissolved organic matter (DOM) coexisting in wastewater, whose impact on FF degradation remains unclear. An efficient advanced oxidation process (AOP) was established by Mn(II), nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA), and peroxymonosulfate (PMS) for degrading the typical aquaculture antibiotic florfenicol (FF), achieving removal efficiency of (97.38±1.02)% within 20 min primarily via Mn(V)=O, in which •OH, •SO4-, and 1O2 made minor contributions. The inhibitory effects of fishery amino acids on FF degradation followed the order: poly lysine > tryptophan > methionine > lysine. Based on electrochemical measurements and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, tryptophan and methionine competed for PMS binding sites, with methionine being preferentially oxidized by Mn(V)=O, thereby delaying FF degradation. Primary degradation pathways involved defluorination, dechlorination, and aromatic ring hydroxylation, exhibiting a reduced toxicity. Overall, this study developed a sustainable strategy to remove typical fishery antibiotics, highlighting the critical role of Mn(V)=O and the interference mechanism of protein-like DOM.

Keywords:

Amino acids; High-valent manganese-oxo species; Nitrilotriacetic acid; Peroxymonosulfate.

title: Effects of artificial electric fields on the physiological state of Amphistegina lessonii: Insights from oxidative stress biomarkers and gene expression.
content:
Abstract

Anthropogenic energy infrastructure, including subsea power cables and renewable devices, introduces unexpected artificial electricity into marine ecosystems, potentially acting as ecological stressors on benthic community. The physiological responses of benthic organisms to electric stimulation remain poorly understood. Benthic foraminifera, single-cell organisms widely used as bioindicators in marine environments, are sensitive to environmental stressors. This proof-of-concept study aims to evaluate the effects of different electric current densities on the benthic foraminiferal species Amphistegina lessonii based on single-cell transcriptomic and biochemical (i.e. proteins and enzymes) analyses in short-term exposure experiments. Electrical stimulation leads to the upregulation of mitochondrial metabolic (COQ3, PPOX, and ATP6) genes, as well as TCA cycle pathways. The biomarkers p-p38 MAPK and p-PKC, which are associated with cellular responses to stressful stimuli, are significantly enhanced at 0.86 μA/cm2, suggesting that this electric density induced a significant physiological response. These responses indicate that electrical stimulation may enhance mitochondrial energy production, potentially increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Following cellular responses to stressful stimuli, antioxidant defence is upregulated as reflected by redox-related (GPX, GGT1) genes. This antioxidant activity is further supported by the levels of multiple biomarkers (GST, GPx, and Se-GPx). This study demonstrates significant metabolic and physiological changes in A. lessonii and its adaptive capability to ensure cell survival under electrical stimulation. These findings also highlight the combined use of cellular biomarkers and single-cell transcriptomic analysis as a promising approach for assessing environmental stress in benthic foraminifera-based biomonitoring.

Keywords:

Biomonitoring; Enzymatic activity; Foraminifera; Reactive oxygen species; Transcriptome.

title: Thermal desiccation and expression of HSP90 and osmotic avoidance protein genes in an acorn barnacle, Amphibalanus amphitrite.
content:
Abstract

The marine intertidal zone (IZ) is ideal for deciphering the organisms' response to thermally desiccated stress during tidal emersion. The distribution of organisms across horizontal and vertical transects is plasticity of thermal adaptation potential. The acorn barnacle, Amphibalanus amphitrite inhabits the upper and mid rocky intertidal zone, often encountering episodic thermal desiccation during inter-tidal emersion. In order to survive, the desiccated organisms endure the heating effect of the rocky substratum and aerial temperature, which leads to body temperature perturbation, coma response, and differential gene expression. The intraday thermal desiccation stress response in A. amphitrite has not been studied in a way that integrates both ecological and molecular responses under natural conditions. This study observed and experimented the various factors in an intraday of monsoon environment, including aerial and substratum temperature, duration of emersion along with ecological responses such as coma response, and gene expression. This is the first study to design and standardise the primer for the gene Osmotic Avoidance protein (OA). The expression of stress genes, heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) and Osmotic Avoidance protein (OA) were carried out using Real-time qPCR among thermally desiccated Amphibalanus amphitrite inhabiting the intertidal zone of Anjuna, Goa, India. The ecological responses revealed compelling insights into the effects of thermal desiccation on barnacles. After a 4 h of exposure, a slight increase in body temperature from 30.5 °C to 31 °C triggered a staggering 50% increase in coma response among the barnacles. The study highlights the dynamic expression levels of HSP90 and OA, which fluctuated significantly with varying degrees of thermal and desiccation stress. Notably, we observed a sharp increase in the combined expression of HSP90 and OA after 4 h, followed by a temporary decrease at 6 h and a HSP90 resurgence at 8 h where the body temperature was the lowest. Such an upregulation of HSP90 suggests temperature-independent and prolonged aerial exposure-mediated regulation of gene expression. Moreover, the declining expression of OA from the 4th to the 8th h of aerial exposure underscores an impressive molecular regulation, suggesting an establishment of osmotolerance among the desiccated barnacles. This research underscores the resilience and adaptability of barnacles, emphasising the need for continued study in the face of climate variability. Expression patterns of HSP90 and OA provide concrete evidence of the existence of thermal and desiccation stress and tolerance mechanisms among A. amphitrite in the IZ.

Keywords:

Amphibalanus amphitrite; Body temperature; Coma response; Desiccation stress; Gene expression; Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90); Intertidal zone; Osmotic avoidance (OA).

title: Evaluating connectivity of fisheries-derived marine debris from northwest African upwelling regions and entanglement exposure risk in the Canary Islands.
content:
Abstract

Marine debris derived from fisheries poses a significant threat to marine biodiversity in the Canary Islands, particularly within ecologically sensitive Special Areas of Conservation (SACs). This study integrates backward Lagrangian trajectory modeling with documented entanglement records to examine the connectivity between potential upstream debris source regions, regional transport pathways, and biological impacts affecting sea turtles and cetaceans in Tenerife, Gran Canaria, and Fuerteventura. A trajectory classification approach was implemented to quantify the proportion of simulated particles intersecting dynamically plausible upstream regions, including the northwest African coastal upwelling system and the Madeira sector. Results revealed seasonally variable connectivity between the archipelago and these regions, highlighting the combined effect of the Canary Current system and wind driven drift in facilitating cross-border debris transport. Entanglement was the most frequently documented impact on sea turtles, and fisheries-related plastic items constituted a dominant component of the debris pool. Although backward trajectory modeling identifies potential connectivity pathways rather than definitive source attribution, the integration of seasonal simulations and observational data supports a spatially explicit assessment of debris exposure risk within protected insular ecosystems. By linking upwelling-driven fisheries activity, fishing-derived ghost gear (ALDFG), regional circulation dynamics, and spatially resolved entanglement patterns within SACs, this study advances an integrated process-based framework applicable to other eastern boundary current systems.

Keywords:

Canary Islands; Cetaceans; Entanglement; Lagrangian modeling; Marine debris; Ocean dynamics; Plastic pollution; Sea turtles.

title: Inventory and risk characterization of urban runoff pollutants in Europe.
content:
Abstract

Urban runoff is a major pathway for chemical pollutants to enter aquatic ecosystems, yet the occurrences and risks of both conventional pollutants and contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) remain poorly characterized. In this study, we analyzed 34 urban runoff samples from multiple European catchment types using a combination of reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RP-LC) and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) for characterization of dissolved organic pollutants, alongside inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) for quantification of trace elements. Street runoff was dominated by heavy metals and tire-derived compounds, including 6PPD-quinone (up to 0.57 µg/L) and 1,3-diphenylguanidine (up to 22.4 µg/L). Benzothiazole-2-sulfonic acid was found in 91% of samples up to 153 µg/L, significantly higher than previously reported concentrations in urban runoff. Several wastewater-associated compounds were also common, suggesting contributions from pharmaceutical residues and public urination in surface runoff, and misconnected pipes in separated sewage networks. Risk assessment revealed several compounds exceeding predicted no-effect concentrations (PNEC) with the highest risk associated with the metals Al (up to 1.1 × 104 times PNEC), Cu (8.9 × 103 times PNEC), and Zn (2.7 × 103 times PNEC). Among CECs, clarithromycin (up to 539 times PNEC), 6PPD-quinone (49 times PNEC), and benzothiazole-2-sulfonic acid (32 times PNEC) posed the greatest risks. Our findings highlight urban runoff as an environmental concern, with metals, pharmaceuticals, and tire compounds as key drivers of ecological risks.

Keywords:

Chemical pollutants; Contaminants of emerging concern; Ecological risk assessment; High-resolution mass spectrometry; Urban runoff.

title: Application of Modified Life's Essential 8 Framework in Sleep Surgery Clinic Patients.
content:
Abstract

Objective:

Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) increases cardiovascular (CV) risk, yet assessments of comprehensive CV health in OSA are limited. This pilot study evaluates CV health among OSA patients through Life's Essential 8 (LE8), the American Heart Association's comprehensive framework evaluating CV health across multiple lifestyle and clinical domains.

Methods:

Patients presenting to our OSA surgery clinic (July 2024-November 2025) were included if data were available for all LE8 components (diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, sleep duration, body mass index [BMI], blood pressure [BP], lipid, and glucose profiles). Composite LE8 scores of < 50, 50-80, and > 80 indicated poor, intermediate, and ideal CV health.

Results:

Fifty-eight patients with OSA (age 58.3 ± 12.1 years; BMI 29.3 ± 4.5 kg/m2; apnea-hypopnea index 31.6 ± 24.7) were included. Most reported weekly exercise ≤ 150 min (53.4%, n = 31) and unhealthy or intermediate dietary quality (74.1%, n = 43). Average non-HDL cholesterol was 116.0 ± 44.5 mg/dL; fasting glucose, 103.6 ± 37.3 mg/dL; HbA1c, 5.7% ± 0.9%; systolic BP, 124.4 ± 18.0 mmHg; diastolic BP, 77.7 ± 8.3 mmHg; and nightly sleep duration, 6.4 ± 1.4 h. Mean composite LE8 score was 64.9 ± 16.1, indicating intermediate CV health. By LE8 score, 12.1% of patients had ideal, 70.7% intermediate, and 17.2% poor CV health.

Conclusion:

Patients within our OSA surgery clinic had intermediate CV health per LE8. Improving modifiable factors, such as diet, physical activity, and sleep duration would raise overall CV health in this population susceptible to elevated CV risk.

Keywords:

Life's Essential 8; cardiovascular health; cardiovascular risk; obstructive sleep apnea; sleep surgery clinic.

title: The study of transdermal delivery mechanism of liposomes using stratum corneum lipid membrane model.
content:
Abstract

A reliable assessment of skin permeation is essential for the rational design of transdermal formulations which effectively deliver active ingredients. In particular, a skin screening platform capable of evaluating skin permeability and elucidating the penetration mechanisms of skin penetration enhancers (SPEs), such as liposomes, is critical for advancing transdermal delivery systems. Here, we developed stratum corneum (SC) lipid membrane models which reproduce the barrier properties of human SC and enable mechanistic study of liposomal transdermal delivery. The models were prepared by annealing ceramide, free fatty acids, cholesterol, and cholesterol sulfate on polycarbonate membranes, forming orthorhombic (OR) and hexagonal (HEX) lipid packing structures representing healthy and impaired barriers, respectively. ATR-FTIR and wide-angle X-ray scattering (WAXS) analyses showed that fatty acid chain length governed lipid packing, with long chains promoting OR and short chains favoring HEX packing structure. Franz diffusion experiments demonstrated permeability trends comparable to those reported for excised human SC, with strong correlations between two systems (Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.869 for kp and 0.943 for tlag). When liposomes permeated through this model, liposomal niacinamide showed markedly enhanced permeation compared to both aqueous and dipropylene glycol (DPG) formulations. Post-permeation FTIR analysis revealed increased orthorhombicity of SC lipids, while complementary elemental analyses suggested that this effect was driven by cholesterol integration into the SC lipids, supporting a vesicle-lipid fusion mechanism. Collectively, this SC lipid membrane model enables quantitative permeability analysis and mechanistic studies of SPEs, supporting the rational optimization of transdermal delivery systems in dermocosmetic and pharmaceutical applications.

Keywords:

Lipid packing; Liposome; Stratum corneum; Transdermal delivery; Vesicle–lipid fusion.

title: Individual and combined ultrasonic-enzymatic treatments for modifying soybean residue (okara) fiber: impacts on structure, physicochemical, and functional properties.
content:
Abstract

This study investigated the effects of ultrasonic, enzymatic, and combined ultrasonic-enzymatic treatments on the structural, physicochemical, and functional properties of soybean residue (okara) dietary fiber (DF). Under the optimal combined ultrasonic-enzymatic treatment conditions, the soluble DF (SDF) yield and water-holding capacity (WHC) of the modified okara DF increased to 8.00 ± 1.04 g/100 g and 14.88 ± 0.29 g/g respectively, representing enhancements of 193.04% and 40.11% compared with unmodified okara DF. Structural analysis showed reduced particle size, a more uniform size distribution, and disrupted microstructures characterized by wrinkles, voids, and fragmentation. Physicochemical properties were also improved (p < 0.05), with WHC, oil-holding capacity (OHC), and swelling capacity (SC) increasing by 40.11%, 82.81%, and 40.19%, respectively. Moreover, the combined treatment exhibited stronger functional effects than individual methods, yielding 4.82- and 10.07-fold increases in cholesterol and bile salt adsorption capacities, and 1.35- and 7.78- fold enhancements in DPPH and hydroxyl radical scavenging activities. These enhancements are attributed to structural modifications, including reduced particle size, increased specific surface area, exposure of functional groups, and decreased crystallinity, which collectively improve the functional properties of okara DF. Overall, this study highlights the synergistic advantages of ultrasonic-enzymatic treatment and provides theoretical and technical support for the high-value utilization of okara DF.

Keywords:

Functional properties; Okara dietary fiber; Physicochemical properties; Structural characteristics; Ultrasonic–enzymatic modification.

title: The Kremlin accidentally published it! Putin will not like it at all.
content:
13:42

The Kremlin accidentally published an unedited version of Vladimir Putin's International Women's Day message; the footage showed Putin coughing for about 30 seconds and moments when he wanted to retake the recording.

A previously unedited section of Russian President Vladimir Putin's speech prepared for International Women's Day was accidentally published. The release of raw footage instead of the edited version that the Kremlin was supposed to share drew attention.

COUGHED FOR 30 SECONDS

In the footage circulating on social media, moments were captured where Putin coughed for about 30 seconds during his speech and then requested that the recording be redone. The video showed Putin stopping the recording and asking for that part of the speech to be recorded again.

VIDEO LEAKED ON THE INTERNET BECAME A TOPIC

Normally, the Kremlin was planning to publish the edited and final version of the speech. However, the mistakenly shared footage included the unedited part of the speech, which quickly became a topic of discussion.

Following the incident, as the footage spread rapidly on social media, it became a matter of curiosity whether the Kremlin would make an official statement regarding the error in the sharing process.

title: Integrated Assessment of Three NDSRIs Through CPCA Prioritization, In Silico Toxicity Assessment, and Stability Indicating LC-MS/MS Method for Avatrombopag Maleate.
content:
Abstract

Avatrombopag maleate (AOG), a thrombopoietin receptor agonist, is a generic drug for which a viable route of synthesis has been identified, in which three nitrosamine drug substance-related impurities (NDSRIs) have been identified. In silico toxicity assessment has been carried out. Being product specific NDSRIs, the specification limit has been defined based on Carcinogenic Potency Categorization Approach (CPCA) approach and selective and sensitive LC-MS/MS-based analytical method developed and validated for their trace level with predefined parameters with results outcome, which are specificity, linearity with r2 between 0.9905 and 0.9999, the LOD as 0.34 ppm, and LOQ as 0.67 ppm for all impurities; the obtained recovery was in the range of 94.0%-105.6% with a SD range between 0.6 and 2.8. The overall mean between the method precision and intermediate precision studies was in the range of 6.43-6.81 ppm, and the overall % RSD for the 12 determinations was between 1.3 and 2.4. The method robustness has also been demonstrated with deliberate variations. The solution stability was studied for about 24 h to assess the nature of the solutions prepared. Further, to assess the fate of each NDSRIs, the sample was inflicted to acid, base, oxidative, thermal, and photolytic stress conditions. This intensive stress study concluded that the identified NDSRIs are carried from the starting material of secondary amine scaffolds in the reaction conditions and not a degradation product. Thus, in this current research work, we revealed three new potential NDSRIs for the AOG drug substance, their toxicity assessment, and CPCA scoring to arrive at the specification limit (Category 3 → AI 400 ng/day → 6.6 ppm as target level). The source of the NDSRI formation has also been demonstrated; finally, their selective, sensitive, and stability indicating LC-MS/MS-based analytical method has been implemented. This wholistic lifecycle approach eliminates the risk-assessment gaps and ratifies the regulatory requirements, thereby endures the product quality and patients safety.

Keywords:

Carcinogenic Potency Categorization Approach (CPCA); LC‐MS/MS method development; NDSRIs; avatrombopag maleate; route scouting; stress degradation.

title: Characterizing soft-bottom epibenthic megainvertebrate communities of the Mediterranean continental shelf: a biogeographic approach
content:
Abstract

Partitioning of the Mediterranean basin has so far mainly focused on surface waters, relying on biogeochemical and hydrological data while the Mediterranean seafloor has received much less attention. Bioregions are essential units for conservation planning, as they provide a framework for designing representative networks of protected areas. Therefore, seafloor-specific bioregions are needed to support the management and conservation of benthic ecosystems. While benthic habitat mapping is generally based on macrofaunal patterns, we propose the first mesoscale partitioning of the Mediterranean seabed based on epibenthic megainvertebrate communities. Benthic records from the MEDITS programme (International Mediterranean Bottom Trawl Survey) were used to partition the Mediterranean soft bottoms. Using k-means clustering combined with Random Forest modelling, we grouped sites according to similarities in biotic composition and predicted their distribution in relation to environmental variables. The analysis was conducted independently across four sub-basins: the Western Mediterranean, the Central Mediterranean, the Adriatic Sea, and the Aegean Sea. This approach identified 16 distinct bioregions, each characterized by unique epibenthic megainvertebrate communities. The partitioning revealed a pronounced bathymetric gradient, with deep-sea bioregions showing a more homogeneous set of indicator taxa and greater similarity across regions compared to the more distinct communities found on the shelf and slope. These coherent bioregions can serve as spatial units to enhance the representativeness of conservation priority networks and provide a valuable complement to the existing EUNIS seabed habitat classification, which does not explicitly account for vulnerable epibenthic megainvertebrate communities.

Keywords:

Bioregionalization; Community structure; Conservation planning; Epifauna; Habitat mapping; K-means; Machine learning; Marine environment; Mediterranean; Megainvertebrates.

title: The U.S. press wrote: Here are 6 possible scenarios awaiting Iran after the war.
content:
13:41

Following the attacks by the U.S. and Israel on Iran, the country's future remains uncertain, while the New York Times, one of the U.S.'s established newspapers, focused on six different scenarios for post-war Iran in its published analysis.

After the attacks initiated by the US and Israel against Iran, a significant uncertainty emerged both in the government ranks and in society. Following the attacks that resulted in the deaths of hundreds of civilians as well as important figures in the Iranian government, the Tehran administration responded to US and Israeli targets across the region.

6 DIFFERENT SCENARIOS CONSIDERED

While the whole world is focused on the region, an analysis published in The New York Times emphasized that the future of approximately 100 million Iranians has become increasingly uncertain with the escalation of conflicts. The analysis discussed six different scenarios that could emerge in Iran after the war.

THE REGIME MAY SURVIVE

According to the analysis, despite the killings of high-ranking officials, the political system in Iran has not completely collapsed. Due to the multi-layered structure of the Revolutionary Guards and state institutions, there is a possibility that the regime may survive. It is also noted that external attacks could strengthen nationalist sentiments in the country, creating a rallying effect around the regime.

THE MILITARY MAY TAKE POWER

According to another scenario, the Revolutionary Guards, the strongest structure in the country after the war, may gain more power. Even if a new religious leader is chosen, it is stated that real political power could be concentrated in the hands of military structures. The analysis also mentions the possibility of a strong military leader emerging.

OPPORTUNITY FOR POLITICAL CHANGE

According to the analysis, for some Iranians, the current crisis is seen as an opportunity for political change in the country. However, the destruction caused by the war and discussions of external intervention create serious uncertainty about how this process will progress.

MONARCHY DISCUSSIONS

While there are discussions in some circles about the potential return of Reza Pahlavi, the son of the Shah who was overthrown in the 1979 revolution, the analysis suggests that it seems quite difficult for a foreign-backed leader to gain legitimacy in Iranian society.

RISK OF REGIONAL CHAOS

The analysis warned that if the Iranian state weakens or collapses, a new wave of instability could arise in the Middle East. It is stated that the fragmentation of a large country like Iran could lead to many issues, from migration crises to arms trafficking.

THE PEOPLE OF IRAN MAY DETERMINE THEIR FUTURE

In the last scenario, it is noted that the economic crisis and social unrest in Iran could trigger political transformation. However, it is emphasized that for this to happen, the war must end, and Iranians should be able to determine their future without external intervention.

title: Dual-targeting strategies for cancer and diabetes: Converging pharmacological pathways and repurposed therapies
content:
Abstract

The rising global burden of cancer and diabetes mellitus, particularly type 2 diabetes (T2DM), underscores a critical need for integrated therapeutic strategies. Epidemiological studies reveal a compelling bidirectional association between these diseases, with T2DM increasing cancer risk and adversely affecting cancer prognosis. Shared pathophysiological mechanisms including insulin/IGF-1 signaling, chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic reprogramming serve as potential therapeutic convergence points. This review explores the mechanistic and clinical basis for dual-targeting strategies that address both malignancy and metabolic dysfunction simultaneously. Key molecular intersections include the PI3K/Akt/mTOR and AMPK pathways, which are central to cell proliferation, survival, and glucose metabolism. Pharmacological agents like metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, and statins demonstrate promising anticancer effects in addition to glycemic control, while biologics such as canakinumab and tocilizumab modulate inflammatory processes relevant to both disease states. Natural compounds including curcumin, resveratrol, and berberine exhibit dual benefits via antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic pathways. The review critically evaluates preclinical studies, retrospective cohort analyses, and clinical trial data supporting the repurposing of anti-diabetic agents for oncology indications. Despite mixed outcomes in large-scale trials, evidence suggests biomarker-based patient selection may enhance therapeutic efficacy. Moreover, emerging paradigms including immunometabolism, gut microbiota modulation, and gene-based interventions offer promising frontiers for integrated care. Ultimately, dual-targeting strategies represent an emerging and promising therapeutic framework for managing patients with overlapping cancer and metabolic disease, with potential to optimize outcomes, reduce therapy-related toxicities, improve long-term survival. Future research must prioritize biomarker-guided precision therapies, multidisciplinary management and the inclusion of metabolic parameters in oncology trial designs.

Keywords:

Cancer; Drug repurposing; Dual-targeting therapy; Immunometabolism; Metformin; PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway; Type 2 diabetes.

title: WAMY Commends Saudi Arabia's Pioneering Model for Women's Empowerment on International Women's Day
content:
Riyadh, March ( وكالة الأنباء السعودية ۔ ‎‎‎ 08 مارس 2026ء) WAMY stated that the Kingdom has presented a pioneering model for empowering women and providing them with opportunities to actively participate in the development process, as women have become essential partners in national development and community work, in line with the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030, which considers women's empowerment a main pillar.

(تستمر)

WAMY noted that its global humanitarian and development programs prioritize women's empowerment by supporting education, vocational training, and capacity building, alongside social welfare programs aimed at mothers and families. These initiatives strengthen women's roles in developing and advancing their societies.

The assembly affirmed that the support and empowerment enjoyed by women in the Kingdom reflect the leadership's wise vision and its belief in the capabilities of Saudi women and their vital role in shaping the future.

title: Children’s Nursery Centers at Two Holy Mosques Provide Safe and Enriching Environment
content:
Makkah, March ( وكالة الأنباء السعودية ۔ ‎‎‎ 08 مارس 2026ء) The centers welcome children around the clock in an environment designed to meet their needs. They offer a variety of educational and cultural programs, as well as recreational activities that support children's sensory, cognitive, social, intellectual, and physical development.

(تستمر)

The authority explained that registration is completed electronically through the designated system or via reception teams on site. Upon arrival, a child’s information is verified and their temperature is checked before entry. Each child is then provided with an identification bracelet containing their details, along with a matching bracelet for their guardian to ensure proper monitoring.

The child is released only after verifying that the information on both bracelets matches the guardian’s details. In the event of loss, the electronically registered data is used for verification.

title: Iran's new religious leader has been chosen! His name will not be disclosed for security reasons.
content:
13:10

Following the assassination of Iran's religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who has been in power since 1989, in a joint operation by Israel and the United States, a new religious leader has been chosen for Iran, but their name will not be disclosed for security reasons.

The war that began with the attack of the USA and Israel on Iran has entered its 9th day. Following Israel's statement, "Everyone who wants to be Khamenei's successor is our target," Iran's new religious leader has been announced. Seyyid Ahmed Alam al-Huda, a member of the 88-member Assembly of Experts in Iran, confirmed that the new leader of Iran has been determined. It was stated that the name of the newly elected religious leader would not be disclosed for reasons.

ASSEMBLY OF EXPERTS OF IRAN: CONSENSUS REACHED ON KHAMENEI'S SUCCESSOR

Mohammed Mehdi Mirbakeri, a member of the Assembly of Experts of Iran, stated that a majority consensus has been reached regarding the successor of the religious leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the attacks by the USA and Israel, but some obstacles related to the process need to be resolved.

ISRAEL: EVERYONE WHO WANTS TO BE KHAMENEI'S SUCCESSOR IS OUR TARGET

The Israeli army announced that any religious leader to be chosen to replace the religious leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the attacks by the USA and Israel, is a target. The statement used was, "Everyone trying to appoint a successor to Khamenei and anyone who will be a successor will be pursued."

SECURITY MEASURE FOR THE NEW LEADER FROM IRAN

Following this warning from Israel, the Iranian Parliament noted that the new religious leader has been elected, but the name will not be disclosed for security reasons for now. Seyyid Ahmed Alam al-Huda stated that the leadership elections in Iran have been held and a leader has been appointed.

According to Al Mayadeen, Alam al-Huda expressed that all rumors and reports suggesting that the Assembly of Experts has not yet made a decision are completely fabricated.

Iranian media reported yesterday, citing a member of the Assembly of Experts, that the Assembly of Experts is expected to convene within 24 hours to elect a new leader following the death of Ali Khamenei.

title: Imam Turki bin Abdullah Royal Reserve Launches Updated Grazing Regulations to Protect Vegetation Cover, Enhance Sustainability
content:
وكالة الأنباء السعودية

4 دقيقة قبل

الأحد مارس | م

Rafha, March ( وكالة الأنباء السعودية ۔ ‎‎‎ 08 مارس 2026ء) The updated regulations organize grazing through official permits and specific temporal and spatial controls, while restricting grazing to designated areas according to their carrying capacity. This prevents random or excessive grazing that leads to soil degradation and the decline of vegetation cover. The regulations also specify the number of livestock permitted for each beneficiary in line with rangeland characteristics, ensuring the rational and sustainable use of grazing lands.

(تستمر)

The updated version also takes into account the social and economic aspects of the local communities, including expanding grazing zones in villages and settlements within the reserve’s boundaries, in addition to introducing grazing belts for areas adjacent to the reserve, while adhering to environmental considerations and relying on relevant scientific studies to ensure the sustainability of natural resources.

It added that environmental protection and monitoring teams oversee the implementation of the regulations around the clock through intensive patrols and modern monitoring systems, with legal measures applied against violators according to the approved regulations. The authority emphasized that organizing grazing represents one of the fundamental pillars of environmental protection within the reserve and achieving the long-term sustainability of rangelands, calling on all beneficiaries to fully comply with the regulations and instructions to preserve natural resources and enhance the reserve’s position as an advanced national model in sustainable environmental management.

title: This Atlanta ministry is doing what most denominations can’t — turning Gen Z into passionate churchgoers
content:
Atlanta, Georgia
  — 

The stage is still shrouded in darkness when a keyboardist opens with a single, solemn note. The musician holds the note, steadily increasing its volume, as onlookers rise from their seats to surge forward.

The auditorium then explodes with a barrage of lights and sounds. Four singers sprint to the foot of the stage, pumping their fists. The band joins them, unleashing a torrent of thunderous drums and scratchy guitar riffs that sound like an arena-rock anthem.

“C’mon! Anyone grateful tonight?” the lead singer bellows as white, red and amber stage lights flicker behind him. Several thousand fans roar in response and join him in a hymn of gratitude by following the song’s lyrics displayed on two screens flanking the stage.

This might look like a concert, but it’s actually church. Yet hardly anyone in the crowd tonight uses that name. They call it “TLR,” or “The Living Room,” and it’s a home away from home for the roughly 2,800 people who packed the auditorium on a recent Monday night. The Living Room was created by North Point Community Church, a nondenominational Georgia megachurch founded by its senior pastor, Andy Stanley.

But the most astonishing sight on this evening is not what’s happening on stage. It comes when a crane camera pans the crowd and flashes a panoramic view of the audience on the screens. Virtually everyone in the audience is a member of Gen Z — those digital natives loosely ranging in age from 14 to 29 who are reportedly the least religious and most socially isolated generation in America.

The audience includes Gen Zers like Logan Everson, 22, who could be seen at the front of the stage, praying out aloud as the band rocked on. Everson didn’t grow up in church but then heard about the TLR via Instagram. He paid his first visit last year.

“When I first started coming, I was up in the balcony, nervous and away from everybody,” says Everson, who has a tattoo of Jesus wearing a crown of thorns inscribed on his left calf. “Once I entered Christ, I started moving down a little bit more. Now, I’m on the front row.”

Conversion stories are usually a cause for celebrations. But the success of North Point and other megachurches like them raise questions — including a troubling one for many of the most prestigious churches in America:

Why are nondenominational megachurches like North Point so good at reaching young Americans? And why are mainline Protestant denominations, like the United Methodist and Episcopal churches, apparently so bad at trying to do the same?

Why it’s hard to reach the ‘anxious generation’

The easy answer is that megachurches are better at attracting young people because they know how to put on a good show. Put any pastor in hip clothes onstage, backed by a rocking band, and young people will materialize.

But that’s an illusion. The people who founded TLR as a Bible study group with 20 students at Georgia Tech say it took years of grinding effort before they could consistently attract 200 attendees. They say you can’t keep Gen Z’s attention through pulpit pyrotechnics alone.

North Point faces the challenge that virtually every American institution – and many parents – confront every day. How do you reach Gen Z and keep their attention?

The challenge is immense. Gen Z is called “the anxious generation.” They’ve never known a world without the internet, smartphones and social media. They are lonelier and more fearful about the future than other generations. Dating and making friends is a struggle. Many, reared on digital screens, have a hard time holding a conversation with another human being.

“Our generation is more connected to social media than ever and that’s a driver of a lot of our mental health problems,” says Katherine Babbitt, a North Point member who joined the TLR before moving away to New York City to work in the finance industry. “You’re so overstimulated from that (social media) that you don’t want to go out, go to church and even sometimes meet up with your friends.”

North Point faces another challenge. All sorts of Americans, not just young people, no longer attend church. This exodus has hit mainline Protestant churches – defined as the seven of some of the oldest and most historically dominant denominations in the US – the hardest. Denominations such as The Episcopal Church and the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) are experiencing an “unremitting collapse” in membership.

Mainline denominations helped make the US a more humane country. They were pivotal in the abolition of slavery and promoting labor rights and civil rights. In recent years they’ve provided the moral leadership for ordaining women as clergy, affirming gay and lesbian people in places of worship, and championing anti-ICE protests in places like Minnesota.

But mainline pastors are performing more funerals than baptisms today, says Ryan Burge, a political scientist who once preached the last sermon at a mainline church that closed due to dwindling membership. In 1975, 30% of all American adults were mainline Protestants; today it’s below 9%. And only 2% of all adults are mainline Protestants under the age of 40, he says.

“There’s an iron law of church growth — if I walk in and there’s more gray hair than children, it’s over,” says Burge, author of “The Vanishing Church.” “There’s really no way to pull out of that tailspin. A lot of churches are lumbering toward extinction.”

There are exceptions. Resurrection, a United Methodist Church with locations in Kansas and Missouri, has built a congregation of some 23,000 members through high-octane worship music, an emphasis on small group meetings and aggressive outreach to young people. It’s the largest United Methodist church in the US.

But Burge says anecdotal research showing that young people are leading an uptick in church attendance does not reflect the larger downward trend he is seeing.

And help is not on the way. Only one-third of US adults between the ages of 18 and 29 say that religion is “very important in their lives” according to a new Gallup poll — down from 47% in the early 2000s.

“Each successive generation is less religious, and there’s really no evidence in the data of Gen Z going back to church or being more religious,” says Burge. “Almost half of them say they never go to church, so what Andy’s (Stanley) church is doing is really weird.”

So how did North Point crack the code for reaching Gen Z?

Stanley and his staff employ two strategies that are largely missing from mainline denominations. One is rooted in the New Testament — and the diverging fortunes of Netflix and Blockbuster Video.

They draw inspiration from ‘seeker’ churches

The man who has overseen North Point’s success with Gen-Z leads an afternoon staff meeting at a modest building in a suburban office complex about 20 miles outside of Atlanta.

Stanley, a lanky man with a laid-back Southern demeanor, is dressed in jeans and a button-down shirt. Staff members on Apple laptops discuss a slick, in-house video slated for an upcoming Sunday service. It playfully depicts exhausted parents trying to muster the energy to attend church.

People bat around sermon tweaks and titles. The vibe in the room is one of a startup business, not a megachurch with an estimated 50,000 weekly attendees and that consistently ranks as among the top five largest churches in the US.

Stanley knows something about reaching tough audiences. He was once voted one of the 12 most effective preachers in the English language in a Baylor University survey, one of the most prestigious honors in the profession. He had a tough act to follow: He’s the son of the Rev. Charles Stanley, a preaching legend who was twice elected president of the Southern Baptist Convention, the largest Protestant organization in the US.

Ask him why his church reaches Gen Z in way that traditional mainline struggle to replicate, and he starts with the preaching. He says many mainline preachers are good pastors but may not be good leaders. And some of their preaching lacks a quality that his father valued.

“My dad used to call it a burden,” Stanley says. “We’d listen to somebody preaching and my dad would say, ‘He has no burden.’ He’s not teaching for life change. He’s content to have covered his material. He’s not driven by the question: Are people getting this, are they applying it, and are their lives changing?”

Stanley’s approach is shaped by the “seeker” church movement that emerged in the 1970s. It was designed to reach Americans who were jaded by organized religion or who grew up in a culture where the Bible no longer carried any authority. The movement’s leaders eliminated many of the trappings that turned people away from church — traditional architecture, robed clergy, hymnals filled with turgid songs from the 19th century and sermons overloaded with abstract religious phrases.

Seeker churches embraced contemporary music and jeans-clad pastors with slick presentations (one commentator described a seeker worship service as a “Coldplay concert followed by a TED talk”). They were more committed to progress than maintaining traditions.

That thinking shapes how North Point attracts young worshippers. Its staff tinkers with worship settings to make them more welcoming. They favor sermons steeped in the New Testament, but light on unnecessary theological jargon and heavy on practical application.

It’s working. North Point estimates that half its community are college students or younger.

Burge says the ministries in America that consistently attract new young members tend to be non-denominational churches.

“If churches like North Point didn’t exist, American Christianity would be in much deeper decline than it is right now,” he says. “They’re drawing in thousands of people who have found a relationship with God and each other.”

‘You date the model but marry the mission’

Most traditional churches lack North Point’s ability to quickly adapt, Stanley says. Their traditions are guarded with ferocious intensity. A change to the Episcopal Church’s “Book of Common Prayer,” for example, could take a decade.

Stanley has a saying that explains his church’s success: “You date the model but marry the mission.”

He cites the example of Blockbuster Video and Netflix. Blockbuster was once the dominant player in home video but was too attached to its model — renting DVDs and VHS tapes in person from retail stores. The company eventually lost out to Netflix, which emphasized the “ministry” — delivering movies and TV shows to consumers in whatever way worked best.

Stanley says this is the same approach that enabled the first Christians to thrive: They dispensed any unnecessary obstacles to taking their message to Gentiles, such as requiring obedience to the Torah.

“Not judging because I don’t know many mainline church leaders, but some of them are married to the model,” he says. “They’re not married to the mission, so consequently they’re not willing to adjust the model. Businesses can’t do this. When a business marries a model, they go out of business.”

Part of that adaptability is how churches bring worship to Gen Z, he says. Instead of waiting for young people to come to church, North Point goes to them. The Living Room, for example, charters up to 14 buses every Monday night that fan across metro Atlanta to pick up college students and take them to and from services. They also buy 270 boxes of cheese and pepperoni pizza to feed them before returning them home.

That kind of service costs money. North Point Ministries devotes 25.67% of its total budget to its family and college ministries. Many mainline churches focus more on older members, who tend to be big donors. The result is that older members’ preferences often dictate how a church operates—young people just can’t afford to give as much. But North Point is a prime example of a church that casts its bread, or pizza, upon the waters: It’s gambling that its generosity will be rewarded one day.

“I’ve been to a lot of other churches, and we (family and youth ministry) were nickel and dimed every Craft material to stay in budget—usually we get the second leftovers,” says Kendra Fleming, executive director of Family Ministry at North Point. “When I came here, they were willing to put their money, their staff, their facilities in a position to reach a group of people who can’t pay for it.”

It’s common to hear North Point staffers repeat a line that Stanley often uses to justify the ministry’s commitment to youth: “What is the next generation worth? Everything.”

There’s a second Stanley adage that also offers insight into North Point’s success in engaging Gen Z.

‘Circles are better than rows’

It’s Monday night again at The Living Room in Atlanta’s Buckhead neighborhood, one of North Point’s eight churches across the area.

The band is still rocking. Sweat pours down the lead singer’s right cheek. A North Point pastor, Matt Noblitt, takes the stage wearing white sneakers and a hoodie emblazoned with a baby-blue ATL logo. The attendees call up their Bible apps as he talks, and their smartphones light up the darkened theater like fireflies on a summer night.

But it’s what Noblitt says at the beginning of the sermon that explains North Point’s success drawing young members.

“This is a big gathering,” he says. “The way that we can make big gathering feel personal, and the way for you to get to know people, and to be known, is for you to get involved in community. So you can sign up for a group if you’re not already in a group.”

In his sermon, Noblitt preaches that being young is being filled with tough questions such as “who am I supposed to date?” and “what career path should I take?” He encourages his young listeners to form a healthy identity and think about what they expose themselves to online.

“What you allow your eyes to see over time,” he says, “I’m telling you, it will impact and influence your life.”

Afterwards, the attendees split into small groups and fan throughout the 190,000-square-foot building to hold small group discussions guided by church staffers. They talk about the sermon’s message and share prayers.

This emphasis on small groups reveals a paradox in North Point’s approach: They got big by focusing on going small.

The church’s community calendar is filled with small groups that meet throughout the week. Members aren’t just gathering to talk about intellectual ideas, like a book club. They’re sharing prayers and struggles, along with confession.

Mainline churches typically center their worship around “rows” — members sitting in pews or rows of chairs to listen to speakers during worship and Bible studies. But Stanley and North Point’s leaders insist that true community comes when people meet face-to-face in circles.

“What we do with small groups is way more important than what happens onstage,” Stanley tells CNN. “Kids can go to concerts anywhere, but where do they sit in a circle with an adult who’s going get into the issues of life with them?”

It turns out that many members of Gen Z are desperate for the community provided by circles.

Everson, the TLR attendee with the Jesus tattoo, talked with enthusiasm about befriending one of the church’s pastors, chatting with him via text and sharing conversations in small groups.

“You can be honest,” Everson says of the cozy gatherings. “You can talk about the sermon, how it changed the way you look at life. It’s less than 15 people, so you can get intimate with people and build community.”

Jontavious McGriff, 19, a Georgia State University student, belongs to one of these small groups. He says it was the message, not the music, that drew him to TLR. He was baptized at TLR last year and says its pastors preach about the consequences of sin but not in the harsh manner of traditional churches.

“A lot of people my age don’t really like church because they feel its judgmental. They can’t connect, and every pastor is coming to get them,” he says. “But this place isn’t judgmental like that at all. Pastor Matt is always like, ‘We’ve all been there. I’ve been there.’ “

North Point also pairs each youth group — from preschool to Gen Z — with spiritual mentors who are not that much older than the kids they counsel.

Babbitt, who grew up in North Point’s youth ministry, says having mentors near her age was crucial. It made Christianity seen normal and appealing.

“For young people who are often insecure, it gives us reassurance of like, they’re cool, they’re normal and I want to be around them and like them,” she says.

The benefits go both ways. Pastors learn what’s on young attendees’ minds, which helps them tailor sermons to address their concerns. Popular sermon topics at TLR include dating, finding one’s personal identity and coping with anxiety over social media.

Noblitt, the longtime TLR pastor, says that what young people want most is an adult who will listen to them.

“What I have learned is that they don’t need me to be the cool, trendy pastor. What they need me to be is someone who cares about them and wants to invest in them,” he says.

“What they need to see in me is that I live out what I’m preaching and that I love my wife. They need to see me be the best dad I can be, and (to see) that I follow Jesus in every area of my life. They don’t care what sneakers I’m wearing.”

A mother’s thanksgiving

Some may not regret the collapse of mainline denominations. But they serve an important purpose: Mainline churches are one of the few communal places left in America where people of differing political beliefs are challenged to find common ground.

Pastors can set the tone. When people ask the Rev. Adam Hamilton, the founder and senior pastor of the Resurrection megachurch, if he’s a liberal or a conservative, he says yes. He’s both. Hamilton’s congregation is that rare mainline church where membership is booming.

“To be liberal means to be generous of spirit, compassionate, and willing to embrace new ideas and change. To be conservative says there are some things that are just true, and we’re going to hold on to and preserve them,” he says.

“If you’re conservative without being liberal, you’re stuck. And if you’re liberal without being conservative, you’re unmoored.”

And when church pews empty, even those who care nothing for religion are hurt, says Robert Putnam, the eminent sociologist and author of “Bowling Alone.” Regular churchgoers are more likely than secular Americans to volunteer, give generously to charity and belong to civic groups.

“Religious institutions have long been the single most important source of community, connectedness and social solidarity in America,” Putnam wrote in his book, “The Upswing: How America Came Together a Century Ago and How We Can Do It Again.”

A church community is what helped Stanley when he was a young man. He struggled with anger issues after his parents’ divorce and had a sometimes contentious relationship with his prominent father before they reconciled through their shared faith.

He’s 67 now and his legacy is set. North Point, founded in the mid-1990s, is now a brand. It keeps generating new members and has a reputation in church circles for attracting top talent to its staff.

So why is he still buying pizza for college students and picking them up with tour buses Monday nights?

“I’m so grateful that I was raised the way I was in terms of being introduced to faith when I was young,” he says. “I’m so grateful for the people I knew when I was in college, who got up in my grill and held me accountable. I’m a better person, husband, father and grandfather, and I want that for everybody. I’m super blessed, lucky, fortunate, entitled — whatever the word is — and I feel like I should do for others what others did for me.”

A sense of gratitude also extends to Everson, the young man with the Jesus tattoo. An only child, he’s found community at North Point and with the older men who hold him accountable. He recently stenciled a Christian cross on his red Ford F-150.

“It’s weird — I look forward to it every Monday night,” Everson says of worship service and the small group meetings afterward. “It’s our living room. It’s the greatest thing that’s ever happened to me.”

His mom, Colleen Everson, has noticed the change. She said her son used to be distant and uncommunicative. He started drinking a bit more. Now he greets her with warmth. He takes food and bottled water to people experiencing homelessness.

“He just seems so much happier now,” she said. “I don’t see the snippiness. I don’t see him being so anxious.”

She then paused mid-sentence and uttered a startling sound that expressed her feelings over the change she’s seen in her son since his baptism.

It was a more powerful testimony than any song or soundbite at TLR’s service.

It was the sound of a mother crying with joy.

John Blake is a CNN senior writer and author of the award-winning memoir, “More Than I Imagined: What a Black Man Discovered About the White Mother He Never Knew.”
